body:
I think that test is pointing to the wrong table.  @CaselIT it's looking for the column named "with_default" so I think it should at least be looking at "computed_default_table" which has that column ?

as for the "default" part, I think this test wants to check that only the column with "server_default" has a "default", but then, if the backend also has "autoincrement" that might also set "default".  So it would also work if we change it to "elif not col.get("autoincrement", False):".     Does cockroachdb put a "default" in the reflected column info but not set "autoincrement" ?      if this SERIAL column generates a new value without the user doing anything, that would qualify as "autoincrement", Postgresql doesn't have true "autoincrement" either but it sets this flag for a SERIAL column.

Hi,
There seem to a conflicting documentation between [`Inspector.get_columns`](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/core/reflection.html?highlight=get_columns#sqlalchemy.engine.reflection.Inspector.get_columns) and the documentation on [`ComponentReflectionTest::test_autoincrement_col`](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/blob/56e817bb0ef4eaca189b42b930a6e99ee4ed0671/lib/sqlalchemy/testing/suite/test_reflection.py#L1111-L1113).
I was working under the assumption that autoincrement was always returned. We should probably fix it (not sure with one is wrong)

As @zzzeek suggested `col.get("autoincrement", False)` would work. Also the inspected table should be `computed_default_table` instead of `computed_column_table` since we are testing that computed is returned not as a default value, but that a default value is still returned if present in other columns.

I think get_columns() has to always have at the very least "autoincrement": "auto" in that dictionary.    oracle, sqlite etc do it.   so there should probably be a compliance test that this key is there.
which means the "autoincrement" check we are doing there is probably not a good idea and we should do what the poster says and look for "id" which we know might have a default :)
We could also just test explicitly that the computed column does not have a default, since that is the actual test we are doing

im all for fixing it :)

@rafiss, you probably should include "autoincrement": "auto" in the columns dictionary at the least.   for a SERIAL col that will generate new values automatically, have it returned as true.

> Does cockroachdb put a "default" in the reflected column info but not set "autoincrement" ?

Yes, the reflected column would have a default of `unique_rowid()`.

> If this SERIAL column generates a new value without the user doing anything, that would qualify as "autoincrement", Postgresql doesn't have true "autoincrement" either but it sets this flag for a SERIAL column

I didn't realize -- in that case, I will make the CockroachDB dialect set `autoincrement`.

Perhaps related: I see that tests marked as requiring `autoincrement_insert` do in fact expect the database to increment values 1-by-1. E.g. `test_autoincrement_on_insert`, `test_native_lastrowid_autoinc`, and `test_autoincrement_on_insert_implicit_returning` all assert that the ID goes up by 1.

> you probably should include "autoincrement": "auto" in the columns dictionary at the least. for a SERIAL col that will generate new values automatically, have it returned as true.

Sounds good to me.


I can also go ahead and modify the test as discussed above. So if I understand correctly, these would be the changes:
* make the test look at `computed_default_table`.
* don't use a for loop and look at autoincrement; instead just check each column by name.

Is that correct?
